criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: one job at a time (drain, or drain_concurrent with bound 1), a queue of one running job plus three more queued items, window 3. While the first job is gated in `run`, the log shows `read` for the next items before `land` of the first job. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead`.
criteria.evidence: I ran the command and both new tests passed: read_ahead_reads_the_next_items_while_a_single_job_runs (a chain a→b→c→d) and read_ahead_reads_independent_items_while_a_single_job_runs (one plan group, which exercises the drain_with split-off). Both use concurrent(&world, 1) with window 3, and a is gated on read b, read c and read d. They assert that each read comes before end a (and, in the chain test, before land a), that every item is read exactly once, that landed == 4 and that widest <= 4. Athena did not run the fails-without demonstration for this criterion. From reading the base code: bound 1 called run_serial, which spawns no pump, so the gate would time out and the read-before-end assertions would fail.

criteria.criterion: A new test with look-ahead limit 1 and the same queue: while the first job runs, exactly one later item is read (`world.count("read c") == 0` and `read b` is logged, or the equivalent for the fake's item names), and the next is read only after the held reading is claimed. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead`.
criteria.evidence: read_ahead_with_a_limit_of_one_reads_one_item_ahead passed in my run. It asserts that the reads logged before end a are exactly [read a, read b], that end a < read c < end b, that each item is read once and that widest <= 2. Athena's fails-without run of this test on the reverted tree exited 101.

criteria.criterion: A new test where the look-ahead reading of a queued item is refused (not runnable or an error) while the first job runs: the batch still lands the first job, the refused item is reported as it is today (same line, or same stop or reading-refused outcome as when read at its turn), and the pump's drop note appears in `report.notes`. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead`.
criteria.evidence: read_ahead_of_a_refused_reading_is_reported_as_when_it_starts passed in my run. It asserts that read b < end a < land a and that the drop note 'the reading made ahead of b was dropped' is in report.notes. It then compares the run against a window-0 run: b's job line (outcome, reason, landing), the stop, the landed count and all notes other than the read-ahead ones are equal. Athena's fails-without run of this test exited 101.

criteria.criterion: The existing read-ahead tests still pass, with `read_ahead_is_off_with_a_bound_of_one` rewritten so that window 0 still means no reading ahead for drain and for drain_concurrent(1). Every item is read after the job before it landed, and `plan_ahead` is never called. Verified with `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
criteria.evidence: read_ahead_is_off_with_a_window_of_zero (drain.rs:5212) covers four cases: drain_concurrent 1 with window 0, drain with window 0, drain_concurrent 2 with window 0, and drain with window 1. In each case it asserts land a < read b, land b < read c, that plan_ahead b is never called and that there is no stale note. All 29 read_ahead_tests passed in my run. For the full suite and clippy I rely on Athena's recorded checks (CI run 42071793087): `cargo test --locked` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` both passed.

criteria.criterion: The module doc in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (the Read-ahead bullet) no longer says nothing is read ahead with one job at a time. It says read-ahead applies there too and is bounded by `Steps::read_ahead`. `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria.evidence: The Read-ahead bullet now opens: 'When [`Steps::read_ahead`] is above 0, with one job at a time as with several, [`drain_concurrent`] also reads…'. It adds that the number held or being made at once is bounded by Steps::read_ahead, and that drain reads each item at its turn because its steps are not Sync. The old sentence 'With one job at a time … nothing is read ahead' is gone. The Steps::read_ahead and drain_concurrent docs were updated to match. Athena's recorded fmt check passed.

findings.summary: Athena did not run the fails-without demonstration for criterion 1.
findings.evidence: The planned command was a compound `&&` command, so Athena skipped it. I could not revert the code myself because my role changes nothing. From reading the base code: drain_concurrent with bound 1 called run_serial, which never spawns read_ahead_pump. The new tests would therefore time out on the gate and fail the read-before-end assertions. The same mechanism was confirmed by the fails-without runs for criteria 2 and 3, which both exited 101.

findings.summary: The refused-reading test pins the exact number of reads that the drain's existing retry rule produces.
findings.evidence: `assert_eq!(turn.count("read b"), 2)` and `ahead.count("read b") == 3` depend on today's rule of trying a refused item once more, as the test comment says. If that rule changes, this test will need updating. It is acceptable as a guard that the look-ahead adds exactly one extra reading.

summary: The change does what was asked: with one job at a time, the drain now reads the next queued items while the current job runs, up to the limit set by `Steps::read_ahead`. It meets all six acceptance criteria, has no blocker or major findings, and I judge it a pass. Before, a bound of 1 skipped the background reader entirely. Now it runs whenever `read_ahead` is above 0. The other items in the running item's plan group are also handed to the reader, which reads them but never starts them as jobs. `athena drain` uses this entry point, so the change reaches the real command, but production behaviour is unchanged for now because the real steps still leave `read_ahead` at 0. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli read_ahead` and all 29 tests passed, including the four new ones. They show: (1) the next three items are read before the first job ends and lands, (2) with a limit of 1, exactly one item is read ahead and the next only after it is taken, and (3) a refused reading made ahead adds a 'dropped' note but is otherwise reported exactly as in a run with no read-ahead, and the current job still lands. The old bound-of-1 test was rewritten so that a limit of 0, and the plain `drain` entry point, still read nothing ahead. Athena's re-runs with the fix reverted made the tests for criteria 2 and 3 fail as they should. For the full test suite, clippy and fmt I rely on Athena's recorded CI results, which all passed. Only drain.rs and CHANGELOG.md changed, and both were expected. The approach reuses the existing read-ahead machinery and its guards (limit, job limit, budget, file overlap, stop), so I have no soundness concerns. Two nits: Athena did not run the fails-without check for criterion 1, and the refused-reading test pins the exact number of reads that today's retry rule produces.
